goal: Learn Kubernetes deeply and pass the CKA exam, including hands-on cluster setup
interpretation: In 45 minutes of viewing, the learner gets a solid, exam-oriented foundation in Kubernetes architecture, core objects, kubectl, and a kubeadm cluster setup overview, plus a clear picture of the CKA exam and what to study next.
assumptions: The 45-minute budget is viewing time only, so hands-on practice and the exam itself are outside it.
The learner wants a foundation and a roadmap for CKA prep, not full exam readiness from videos alone.
The learner is targeting the current CKA curriculum (cluster architecture, workloads, services and networking, storage, troubleshooting).
Exam-prep oriented means videos that mention the CKA domains, exam tips, or kubectl speed and imperative commands, not generic overviews.
feasibility_note: Learning Kubernetes deeply and passing the CKA cannot be done in 45 minutes; the exam needs dozens of hours of hands-on practice. What is realistic is a CKA-oriented foundation: architecture, pods, deployments, services, kubectl usage, a kubeadm setup walkthrough, and an exam overview with a study roadmap.

sub_topics.title: CKA exam format, domains and study strategy
sub_topics.why: The learner needs to know what the exam covers and how it is graded (performance-based, in a terminal) to focus on the right material.

sub_topics.title: Kubernetes architecture: control plane and worker node components
sub_topics.why: Knowing Docker on single servers, they need to see how API server, etcd, scheduler, controller manager, kubelet and kube-proxy orchestrate containers across nodes. This is a core exam domain.

sub_topics.title: kubectl essentials and imperative commands for the exam
sub_topics.why: kubectl is the sole interface in the exam; speed with imperative commands, YAML generation (--dry-run=client -o yaml) and contexts is critical.

sub_topics.title: Pods, ReplicaSets and Deployments
sub_topics.why: They already know containers, so they can map containers to pods and learn scaling, rolling updates and rollbacks, which are heavily tested workload topics.

sub_topics.title: Services and networking basics (ClusterIP, NodePort, DNS)
sub_topics.why: Moving from Docker port mapping to Kubernetes service abstractions is a major conceptual step and an exam domain.

sub_topics.title: Cluster setup with kubeadm
sub_topics.why: Hands-on cluster installation and bootstrapping with kubeadm is explicitly part of the CKA and of the learner's goal.

picks.reason: A short first-person CKA walkthrough covering exam format, the 2025 changes, study strategy, practice labs and mock exams, and exam-day tips. It gives the learner the exam roadmap before the technical material starts, which suits the exam-prep constraint.

picks.reason: A 'CKA Ch 1.1' explainer on control plane and worker node components (API server, etcd, scheduler, controller manager, kubelet, kube-proxy). picks.title: Day 13: Imperative commands for Deployments, Services and Troubleshooting | CKA Course 2025
picks.reason: A CKA-series lesson on imperative kubectl: creating a Deployment and exposing it with a Service, using --dry-run to generate YAML, and temporary test pods. The selected chapters (backend Deployment, then backend Service) teach the speed-oriented workflow the exam rewards and cover the Deployment and ClusterIP-service basics in one codebase.

evidence.quote: We’ll create the frontend and backend stacks using imperative commands, demonstrate how to quickly generate YAML manifests, and learn how to create test pods for connectivity and debugging.

picks.title: How Kubernetes Heals Itself: ReplicaSets Explained
picks.reason: Explains why a standalone pod is not self-healing and how a ReplicaSet uses labels and selectors to keep the desired pod count. It shows a ReplicaSet YAML, applying it, and deleting a pod to watch it return. This fills in the ReplicaSet layer beneath Deployments, which the imperative video only uses implicitly.

evidence.quote: Today we give the fleet a written order, and Kubernetes brings lost pods back all by itself.
Labels and selectors: how a ReplicaSet knows which pods to count
Delete a pod and watch it come back

picks.confidence_note: Chapters are detailed and match the topic, but there is no transcript and the video is not CKA-framed.

picks.title: Setup Kubernetes Cluster Using Kubeadm [Multi-node]
picks.reason: Builds a multi-node cluster with kubeadm (one control plane, two workers). The selected part covers the kubeadm workflow and the cluster setup itself, so the learner sees init and join in practice and ties it back to the architecture components. The metrics-server and kubeconfig sections are skipped to save budget.

evidence.quote: In this video, you will learn to set up a multi-node kubernetes cluster using Kubeadm with one master and two worker nodes.

None of the 36 candidates has a transcript, so every pick is judged from chapter lists and descriptions. Confidence is moderate at best, so skim the first minute of each video to confirm it matches.

The goal of learning Kubernetes deeply and passing the CKA cannot be met in 45 minutes. This plan gives an exam-oriented foundation (about 42.8 of 45 minutes). Passing needs dozens of hours of hands-on practice, for example killer.sh and killercoda.

Services and networking is only partly covered, through creating a ClusterIP Service in the imperative video. NodePort details and cluster DNS are not explicitly covered. Add yL_DurdVxak (NodePort for CKA) or a services video when you have more time.
Storage, RBAC, troubleshooting and etcd backup are outside the 45-minute plan but are CKA exam domains. The freeCodeCamp CKA course is a natural next step.
The exam-overview pick (SuKkL8YjXMg) is a short personal account and may be shallow. Check the current CKA curriculum on the Linux Foundation site.
Order assumption: the plan puts kubectl before pods, so the imperative-commands segment comes before the ReplicaSet video, which explains the layer underneath Deployments.
